name.text: Trigonometric Functions — exact value at a standard angle

questiontext.text:
Find the exact value of \( [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos[[else]]\tan[[/if]]({@angledeg@}^\circ) \).

Give an exact answer, not a decimal. Type \(\sqrt{3}\) as sqrt(3).

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
To find a trigonometric ratio of an angle beyond \(90^\circ\), use its reference angle (the acute angle it makes with the \(x\)-axis) for the size, and the quadrant for the sign.

  • \({@angledeg@}^\circ\) lies in quadrant {@quadrant@}, and its reference angle is \({@refangle@}^\circ\). So \(\left|[[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos[[else]]\tan[[/if]]({@angledeg@}^\circ)\right| = [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos[[else]]\tan[[/if]]({@refangle@}^\circ) = {@abs(ta)@}\).
  • The signs by quadrant are: all three positive in quadrant 1; only sine positive in quadrant 2; only tangent positive in quadrant 3; only cosine positive in quadrant 4. In quadrant {@quadrant@}, [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]sine[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]cosine[[else]]tangent[[/if]] is [[if test="is(ta>0)"]]positive[[else]]negative[[/if]].

So \( [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]\sin[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]\cos[[else]]\tan[[/if]]({@angledeg@}^\circ) = {@ta@} \).

questionnote.text: fn {@fn@} (0 sin, 1 cos, 2 tan) at {@angledeg@} degrees = {@ta@}

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.9 (Trigonometric Functions). Exact value of sin, cos or tan at a standard angle beyond the first quadrant; catches getting the magnitude right via the reference angle but the sign wrong for the quadrant. sin, cos and tan are forbidden in the answer, so the CAS cannot evaluate it for the student.

node.description: Correct exact value with the right sign

truefeedback.text: The size of your answer is right, but check the sign. Which quadrant is \({@angledeg@}^\circ\) in, and is [[if test="is(fn=0)"]]sine[[elif test="is(fn=1)"]]cosine[[else]]tangent[[/if]] positive or negative there?

falsefeedback.text: Find the reference angle (the acute angle to the \(x\)-axis) and use the exact value for that angle. Then fix the sign from the quadrant the angle is in.
